subs: Beds on its Medicare cost report. A licensed bed count usually runs higher.
Every intensive and special care unit counts: adult, cardiac, surgical, burn, neonatal and pediatric.
Each inpatient stay that ended counts once, whoever paid for it.
All inpatient days divided by discharges. Answer in days, like 4.5.
Patient days divided by the bed days it had available.
Medicare Advantage plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Medicaid managed care plans included. Counted in days spent in a bed, not in people.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payroll only: not clinics, not contract staff.
Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.
From AHRQ's 2023 list of who owns which hospital, matched to Medicare's hospital list.
Out of every hospital in New Hampshire on Medicare's list, every kind counted.
Small rural hospitals with 25 inpatient beds at most, paid by Medicare on their costs.
Every one of its hospitals' latest Medicare cost report, added up.
Biggest by beds on its cost report. The answer names the hospital.
Two half-time employees count as one. Hospital payrolls only: clinics, offices and any health plan are left out.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Concord Hospital have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: No other Capital Region Health Care hospital reports more; Concord Hospital- Laconia is next at 713. About 14.2 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Concord Hospital- Laconia have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Capital Region Health Care hospitals; Concord Hospital has the most, 2,930. About 8.3 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees did Concord Hospital- Franklin have on its payroll in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Capital Region Health Care hospitals; Concord Hospital has the most, 2,930. About 5.7 for every bed.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians trained at Concord Hospital in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: Interns and residents: doctors training after medical school. Two half-time count as one.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent employees do Capital Region Health Care's hospitals have on payroll, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: How many full-time-equivalent resident physicians train in Capital Region Health Care's hospitals, added together?
questions.why: One of its hospitals reports residents; Concord Hospital trains the most, 26.

questions.q: What percent of Concord Hospital's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: No other Capital Region Health Care hospital runs higher; Concord Hospital- Franklin is next at 46 percent. Traditional Medicare was 33 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 24 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Concord Hospital- Laconia's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: That is the lowest of 3 Capital Region Health Care hospitals; Concord Hospital runs highest, 57 percent. Traditional Medicare was 44 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 0 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Concord Hospital- Franklin's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Capital Region Health Care hospitals; Concord Hospital runs highest, 57 percent. Traditional Medicare was 46 percent and Medicare Advantage plans 0 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Concord Hospital's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicaid was 2 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 12 percent.

questions.q: What percent of Concord Hospital- Laconia's inpatient days in fiscal 2024 were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Traditional Medicaid was 1 percent and Medicaid managed care plans 0 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Capital Region Health Care's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicare patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 44 percent.

questions.q: Across all of Capital Region Health Care's hospitals, what percent of inpatient days were for Medicaid patients?
questions.why: Across every U.S. hospital's cost report it is 24 percent.

questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Capital Region Health Care hospitals; Concord Hospital has the most, 206 beds.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds did Concord Hospital- Laconia report to Medicare for fiscal 2024?

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Concord Hospital report for fiscal 2024?
questions.why: No other Capital Region Health Care hospital discharged more; Concord Hospital- Laconia is next at 3,264. About 32 a day.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Concord Hospital- Laconia report for fiscal 2024?

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Concord Hospital- Franklin report for fiscal 2024?
questions.why: That is the fewest of 3 Capital Region Health Care hospitals; Concord Hospital discharged the most, 11,774. About 1 a day.

questions.q: How many days did the average inpatient stay last at Concord Hospital in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: That ranks second of 3 Capital Region Health Care hospitals; Concord Hospital- Franklin ran longest, 11.1 days. Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: How many days did the average inpatient stay last at Concord Hospital- Laconia in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: That is the shortest of 3 Capital Region Health Care hospitals; Concord Hospital- Franklin ran longest, 11.1 days. Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: How many days did the average inpatient stay last at Concord Hospital- Franklin in fiscal 2024?
questions.why: No other Capital Region Health Care hospital kept patients longer; Concord Hospital is next at 5.5 days. Across the cost reports of U.S. general hospitals it averages 5.0 days.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2024, what percent of Concord Hospital's beds had a patient in them?
questions.why: No other Capital Region Health Care hospital ran fuller; Concord Hospital- Laconia is next at 46 percent.

questions.q: On an average day in fiscal 2024, what percent of Concord Hospital- Franklin's beds had a patient in them?

questions.q: How many hospitals does Capital Region Health Care run, by the federal list of health systems?
questions.why: All of them are in New Hampshire. A system's own count can differ: it may count campuses on their own, or hospitals that joined after 2023.

questions.q: What percent of the hospitals in New Hampshire belong to Capital Region Health Care?
questions.why: 3 of 28. The next biggest system there, Dartmouth-Hitchcock, has 5.

questions.q: How many of Capital Region Health Care's hospitals are critical access hospitals?
questions.why: They are Concord Hospital- Franklin.

questions.q: How many beds do Capital Region Health Care's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: How many beds does Capital Region Health Care's biggest hospital report to Medicare?
questions.why: It is Concord Hospital. Concord Hospital- Laconia is next, with 86.

questions.q: How many intensive care beds do Capital Region Health Care's hospitals report to Medicare, added together?
questions.why: That is 9 percent of their 317 beds. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.

questions.q: How many inpatient discharges did Capital Region Health Care's hospitals report in a year, added together?
questions.why: About 42 a day. From all 3 hospitals' latest cost reports, mostly 2024.
